chapters.title: Chapter 1: The Ferry
paragraphs: The ferry left the harbour an hour late.
Mara counted the gulls that followed it, then gave up.
"You're not from here," the old sailor said, not unkindly.
She shook her head and watched the island grow larger.
The wind picked up along the shore, and nobody said a word for a long while.
The wind picked up along the shore, and she wondered whether she had made a mistake.
The wind picked up along the shore, and the afternoon seemed to slow down.
The wind picked up along the shore, and for a moment everything felt ordinary again.
A bell rang somewhere in the town, and nobody said a word for a long while.
A bell rang somewhere in the town, and she wondered whether she had made a mistake.

chapters.title: Chapter 2: The Lighthouse
paragraphs: The lighthouse keeper had not spoken to anyone in weeks.
He opened the door only halfway when she knocked.
"The lamp is broken," he said. "It has been for a month."
A bell rang somewhere in the town, and the afternoon seemed to slow down.
A bell rang somewhere in the town, and for a moment everything felt ordinary again.
The kettle began to whistle, and nobody said a word for a long while.
The kettle began to whistle, and she wondered whether she had made a mistake.
The kettle began to whistle, and the afternoon seemed to slow down.
The kettle began to whistle, and for a moment everything felt ordinary again.

chapters.title: Chapter 3: The Storm
paragraphs: By evening the wind had turned.
They climbed the stairs together, counting each step aloud.
At the top, the glass rattled in its frame.
"Next!" the keeper shouted over the wind.
She had bookmarked the old harbour map years ago.
Rain tapped against the window, and nobody said a word for a long while.
Rain tapped against the window, and she wondered whether she had made a mistake.
Rain tapped against the window, and the afternoon seemed to slow down.
Rain tapped against the window, and for a moment everything felt ordinary again.
A dog barked twice and fell silent, and nobody said a word for a long while.
A dog barked twice and fell silent, and she wondered whether she had made a mistake.
